label: Ilsa Roon, late runs — testimony by name

purpose.value: Ilsa makes her last honest attempt in the only language she has left — names: the realms have been at peace ten thousand years, the people he kills have families and memories, and the children now practice being afraid of him.

emotionalProgression.note: She no longer explains, she testifies; the gentleness is now effortful, visibly chosen.
'They hold evacuation drills when your amulet glows. The children practice quietly, so as not to frighten the younger children.'

notes: The escalation endpoint for the names arc — and her boundary is load-bearing: she grieves, she accuses, and she still does not call him a monster, only wrong; sympathy curdles to grief, never contempt. The last honest attempt. The hero's reply will still be some variant of 'At last, the enemy respects me.' — that framing belongs to his side of the exchange (notes only), never to an NPC line. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
